brief: Trump publicly pushed Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang; hours later the board did, calling the move cleared by senior US government levels and posing no national security risk, reversing chairman Harvey Jones's denial from days earlier. NVDA jumped up to 30% premarket, S&P futures rose 4.6% and Nasdaq futures were halted. Goldman's Privorotsky had argued before the news that White House support for Huang, not the weekend's Asian stabilization measures, would signal the "Trump market put" is back, while cautioning that DOJ/SEC export-control investigations stay active and the real test is whether offshore data-center licenses get granted. He frames the rally as positioning-driven: 1st-percentile net leverage, record Goldman Panic Index, VIX near 40, and fresh shorts as the "missing ingredient" for a squeeze. Separately he argues the Fed is its most hawkish since 2023, making real rates too high, and draws a 2018 analog: whether this is a genuine bottom or just short covering depends on credit, specifically whether neocloud spreads follow Nvidia. Junk bonds just had their worst 2026 blowout and Gartner expects most neoclouds to fold. Conclusion: the Trump put worked; the Fed put has not shown up.
